---
title: Playback IDs and tokens
description: How a viewer reaches a video through a playback ID, why a private one needs a token your backend signs, and what revoking either does.
icon: KeyRound
---

A viewer never sees a video's `ast_…` ID. They play a **playback ID**, and
for a private video they also need a **token**: proof, signed by your
backend, that your app let this viewer watch this video for a while.

## Playback IDs

A playback ID, `pid_…`, is the handle in a playback URL:

```txt
https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/master.m3u8   private
https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/master.m3u8           public
```

- **Private or public.** Its `policy` is `signed` (plays only with a token)
  or `public` (plays for anyone with the URL). A new video gets one
  playback ID with the `playback_policy` you asked for, `signed` by default.
- **Several per video.** Add one with `POST /v1/assets/{id}/playback-ids`,
  up to 1000 per video. A video can have private and public IDs at once,
  for example a public one for a trailer page and a private one for paying
  viewers. Share links each make their own private ID.
- **Revocable one at a time.** `DELETE /v1/assets/{id}/playback-ids/{pid}`
  stops that ID; the video's other IDs keep playing.
- **Cheap.** A playback ID points at the video, not at files, so adding or
  revoking one copies or moves nothing.

Each playback ID in the asset has a `status` (`active`, `revoking`,
`revoked`) and `playable`, which is `false` until the video has an output
and again once the ID is revoked.

### What revoking does, and how fast

The revoke call answers `200` with `revoked` once the ID is unpublished, or
`202` with `revoking` while ClipMux is still unpublishing it. After that,
every request for the ID answers `404`, including from players that are
already watching, and existing tokens for it stop working.

With built-in delivery, a revoked ID stops at once. With
[Cloudflare edge delivery](/docs/self-host/delivery/cloudflare), the edge
caches route records for up to 60 seconds, so a revoked ID stops within a
minute.

To stop everything for a video, delete it: its playback stops at once.

## Tokens

A token is an ES256 JWT that your backend signs with your app's signing key.
It goes in the URL path, so every playlist, segment and key URL the player
follows carries it without any player hooks.

| Claim | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sub` | The playback ID it is for. A token for one ID can't play another. |
| `aud` | `v` plays the video: playlists, segments, tracks, the poster and the decryption key. `t` fetches only the poster, so a catalogue can show posters for videos a viewer can't play yet. |
| `iat`, `exp` | Issued and expiry times, in whole seconds. |
| `vid` | Optional. A stable ID for the viewer, used to count unique viewers. ClipMux stores only a keyed hash of it. |

The header's `kid` names the signing key. A token signed by another app's
key is refused, even for a valid playback ID.

### Lifetime

`exp - iat` may be at most `max_token_lifetime_seconds`, from `GET /v1/app`:
7 days unless the server's owner changed it. A token issued more than 60
seconds in the future is refused too.

Keep tokens short and let the player renew them: `<clipmux-player>` asks
your backend for a new token when the old one expires, and resumes where it
was. Players ClipMux doesn't control, such as iOS before 17.1 and
AirPlay, can't renew mid-video, so sign their tokens for longer. See
[Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens).

When a token is refused, delivery says why:

- `401 token_expired`: `exp` has passed. Get a new token.
- `403 denied`: the signature, key, playback ID, audience or lifetime is
  wrong. A new token signed the same way won't help.
- `404`: the playback ID doesn't exist, is revoked, or its video has no
  output yet.

### Why signing is local

ClipMux keeps only your signing key's public half. Your backend signs with
the private half, on its own, after your own code has decided the viewer may
watch, and delivery checks the signature when the player asks. So there is
no call to ClipMux per play, ClipMux never needs to know who your users
are, and playback keeps working if your backend can't reach the API.

### Revoking and rotating signing keys

- **Revoking** a signing key ends every token it signed: built-in delivery
  refuses them at once, the Cloudflare edge within a minute. Do this if the
  private key leaks.
- **Rotating** adds a new key and retires the old ones once the longest
  token they may have signed has expired, so no viewer is cut off. Use
  `clipmux admin rotate-signing-key --app NAME` on the server.

`GET /v1/app` lists the keys that still verify tokens, newest first, in
`signing_keys`. See [Rotate keys and secrets](/docs/self-host/operate/rotate-secrets).
